problem_description: Compute the average of total magnetic energy of the system of iron atoms which are arranged in a BCC lattice structure with lattice constant of 2.8665 Å, and a simulation box of dimensions 12 * 12 * 12 (in metal units). The PBC applied in all directions. Each iron atoms should have a mass of 55.845 amu and an initial magnetic moment of magnitude 2.2 μB aligned along the -x-direction. The interatomic interactions must modeled using a hybrid overlay potential that combines an embedded atom method (EAM) potential (Mishin 2006) for atomic interactions, a Heisenberg-type exchange interaction for spin coupling with cutoff 3.4, and long-range dipole–dipole interactions with cutoff 8.0 treated using an Ewald summation scheme (ewald/dipole/spin) with a precision of 10⁻⁴. The system should initialized at a temperature of 100 K with velocities drawn from a Gaussian distribution. The spin dynamics should evolve using a precession integrator with cubic anisotropy, while a Langevin thermostat for spins is applied at 0 K to control spin fluctuations. Atomic motion (lattice moving) is integrated using the NVE ensemble combined with spin dynamics. A timestep of 0.1 fs is used for stable integration of both lattice and spin degrees of freedom. The simulation executed for 1000 steps.
